title: Vision Transformer
description: Image classification backbone applying standard transformer encoders directly to patch sequences.
name: Vision Transformer
summary: Vision Transformers (ViT) split images into non-overlapping patches, flatten and linear-project them into patch embeddings, add positional encodings, and feed them directly into a standard Transformer encoder.
use_when: Working with massive image datasets where global context and scaling limits outperform standard CNNs.
avoid_when: Data budget is small, as ViTs lack the inductive spatial bias of convolutions and overfit easily.
pros: Captures global long-range relationships across pixels immediately from the first layer.
Scales better than CNNs on massive datasets (e.g. JFT-300M).
Unified architecture makes multimodal models (text + image) simple to construct.
cons: Lacks spatial inductive bias, requiring massive datasets or strong regularization to generalize.
Quadratic patch interaction costs make high-resolution imaging expensive.
Higher memory footprint during training compared to CNNs.

key_hyperparams.name: patch_size
key_hyperparams.note: Size of non-overlapping image patches to create. Common choice is 16x16 pixels.

quick_start:
from torchvision.models import vit_b_16, ViT_B_16_Weights
import torch

weights = ViT_B_16_Weights.DEFAULT
model = vit_b_16(weights=weights)
model.eval()
x = torch.rand((1, 3, 224, 224))
out = model(x)
